principles.prompt: Kings face each other with one empty square between them. Who has the opposition?
principles.answer: The side NOT to move. They can hold the face-off; the mover must give way.

principles.prompt: What does having the opposition actually let you do?
principles.answer: Force the enemy king to step aside, then advance into the squares he gave up.

principles.prompt: You're escorting a pawn. What leads — king or pawn?
principles.answer: The king. A pawn move is a spare tempo: save it for the moment it hands the face-off back to your opponent.

principles.prompt: You're defending against king + pawn. Where does your king belong?
principles.answer: In the pawn's path, mirroring the enemy king — when he slides sideways, you slide with him.

demos.title: Win the stand-off
demos.intro: Kings face off on the e-file. Black must move — White has the opposition.

steps.note: Black gives way. Watch White's king walk into the gap.
Not the pawn — the king. White advances on the side Black left open.
Black hurries back to block the path.
White retakes the opposition. Black must give way again.
The same story, one rank higher.
The king walks in. The pawn will stroll home behind him.

demos.title: The spare tempo
demos.intro: Kings face off, but it's White to move — the wrong way around. The pawn fixes that.

steps.note: The kings haven't moved, yet everything changed: now Black must give way. A quiet pawn move passed the obligation across.
— and White's king goes around the other side. From here the e-pawn walks home.

tests.title: Face-off on the d-file
tests.intro: White's king wants to march up the board ahead of his pawn. Hold him back.

wrong.Ke6: White outflanks on the far side with Kc5 and gets in front of his pawn. Meet him head-on down the d-file instead.
wrong.Kc6: White outflanks on the far side with Ke5 and gets in front of his pawn. Meet him head-on down the d-file instead.
wrong.Kd8: Too passive — White plays Kd5, in front of his pawn, and wins. Block him now, while the face-off is still yours to take.

hints: White's king is headed for c5, d5 or e5. One move bars all three routes at once.
Kd6 — take the opposition, directly facing his king.

tests.explanationAfter: Face the king and keep facing it. Each time White sidesteps, you mirror him — he can never reach the squares in front of his pawn, and the pawn can't promote without its king leading the way.

tests.title: Find the face-off
tests.intro: The kings aren't facing each other yet. Get in White's way before his king advances.

wrong.Kd6: White slips past with Kb5 and escorts the pawn from in front. Face his king on the c-file.
wrong.Kc7: One square short — White takes c5, in front of his pawn, and wins. Step all the way up to c6.
wrong.Kd8: White walks to b5 or c5 unchallenged. Get your king into his path now.

hints: His king is on c4. Which square faces it with one square between?
Kc6 — take the opposition before his king moves up.

tests.explanationAfter: You found the face-off and kept it: when his king slid to b4, yours slid to b6. As long as you hold the opposition, his king stays behind his pawn — and a pawn without its king in front can't win.

tests.title: Take the opposition
tests.intro: White to play. Use the opposition to escort the pawn.

wrong.Kf3: Retreating gives up the opposition — Black's king walks forward.

hints: Which square puts your king directly in front of Black's king with one square between?
Kd4 or Kf4 both take the opposition.

tests.explanationAfter: Whenever the kings face each other with one square between, the side NOT to move has the opposition.

tests.title: Lead with the king
tests.intro: Black to play. Your king leads, the pawn follows — same trick, other direction.

wrong.Kd6: Retreating gives up the opposition — White's king walks forward.
wrong.Kf6: Retreating gives up the opposition — White's king walks forward.

hints: Your pawn can't outrun the king — your own king must clear the road first.
Kd5 or Kf5 both take the opposition.

tests.explanationAfter: Sidestep, force White's king to commit, then push the pawn at the moment the pawn move itself returns the opposition to you. King first, pawn second.
